summary.text: Dina Titus is the Democratic incumbent for Nevada's 1st Congressional District, which she has represented since 2013 after one earlier term in the House (2009-2011). A political scientist, she taught at UNLV for decades and served in the Nevada Senate, including as minority leader, before entering Congress. She is campaigning on affordability.

paragraphs.text: Born in Thomasville, Georgia, and grew up in Tifton, Georgia, according to Ballotpedia; her official biography says she grew up in Tifton with her parents and a younger sister.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the College of William and Mary, a master's degree from the University of Georgia, and a doctorate from Florida State University.

Taught American and Nevada government and political science classes at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, from 1979 until her retirement in 2011; her official biography describes her as a non-fiction writer known for expertise on the history and policy of nuclear power, weaponry and waste.
Served in the Nevada Senate representing District 7 for 20 years until 2008, including as Senate Minority Leader from 1993 to 2009 according to her official biography.

Won election to the U.S. House from Nevada's 3rd District in 2008 and lost re-election in 2010 to Joe Heck by less than one percentage point; she then won the 1st District seat in 2012 and has been re-elected since, including in 2024.

Sits on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, where her official biography says she is ranking member of the Subcommittee on Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials, and on the Foreign Affairs Committee (2025-2026).

Her official biography describes her as dean of Nevada's congressional delegation, vice chair of the Hellenic Caucus, a founding member of the Colorado River Caucus, and a longtime opponent of nuclear waste storage at Yucca Mountain; it says she introduced legislation to ban bump stocks after the Las Vegas shooting and played a role in the Brightline West high-speed rail project.
According to her official biography, she has been married to UNLV professor Thomas C. Wright for more than 40 years.
